The Jinn as a Mirror to the Unconscious Desires

The presence of a jinn in the dream world acts as a reflective surface for the unconscious desires and the untapped potential that resides within us. These ethereal beings, often associated with power and hidden knowledge, challenge the dreamer to acknowledge and engage with the deeper desires that have been relegated to the shadows of the subconscious. Dreaming of a jinn is an invitation to confront and integrate these aspects, recognizing them as powerful allies in the journey of self-discovery and fulfillment.

Transformation and the Fluidity of Being

The shape-shifting nature of the jinn symbolizes the fluidity of our identities and the transformative power of self-awareness. Just as jinn can change their form, so too can we transform our selves through insight, growth, and the embrace of our multifaceted nature. This dream encourages the embracing of change, highlighting the transformative journey of becoming that is inherent to the human experience. It is a call to embrace the fluidity of being, to allow for transformation and to find strength in the adaptability and resilience of the self.

Guardianship of Secrets and the Unknown

A jinn appearing in your dream may also serve as a guardian of secrets and the keeper of the unknown. This figure represents the mysteries that lie within us and the secrets of the universe that we have yet to uncover. It invites the dreamer to delve into the depths of their own mystery, to seek out the knowledge that lies hidden, and to respect the sanctity of the unknown. The jinn challenges us to pursue wisdom with reverence and humility, acknowledging that some secrets may be meant to guide us rather than be fully understood.

Dream of the sun's rays and the interpretation of the sun's rays in a dream

Sunlight in a dream has many meanings, as the sun's rays in a dream indicate guidance to what is right and distinguishing truth from falsehood, and the light of the sun in a dream indicates sustenance and success according to the position of the seer and the context of the vision. Among the cases of seeing the sun's rays in a dream:

Ibn Sirin says that the light of the sun in a dream indicates the sustenance that the seer will receive, and it will be great and abundant sustenance.

The sun's rays in a dream indicate the prestige of the ruler or the prestige of the master of the house. Seeing the strength of the sun's rays in a dream indicates the power of the ruler in those countries or the power of the father in his house.

As for seeing the faint or light rays of the sun in a dream, this indicates the disappearance of the prestige attributed to it from what we have mentioned.

sun's rays in a dream

Looking at the sun's rays in a dream indicates the dominance of the seer over his family or people according to his destiny.

The sun's rays in a dream also indicate the justice of the king or the justice of the master of the house, and whenever the sun's light is strong in a dream without harm; Indicates the justice of the shepherd, and vice versa.

And whoever sees the sun's rays in a dream on his head only, attains elevation among people and authority over them.

Sheikh Al-Nabulsi says that the sun's rays in a dream if they are on the chest but not the body, indicate disease.

But if the sun's rays are scorching in a dream, and the sleeper sees that the sun's rays burn his surroundings; This indicates liquidation in the entourage of the ruler, or indicates that the owner of the order in the house expels some of his family and gets rid of them.

One of the symbols of the sun's rays is also that it indicates the disclosure of the secret if the dreamer is trying to hide it or is reassuring to conceal it.

And seeing the light of the sun at night if there is no harm in it indicates goodness and guidance in the place of seeing the sun's rays.

As for the one who looks at the sun until his tears fall in a dream, this indicates fear of Allah Almighty and turning to Him.

Interpretation of the eclipse of the sun in a dream and the veil of the sun

A solar eclipse in a dream generally indicates an accident that affects the ruler or the head of the house, and a lunar eclipse is an accident for the minister or the person in charge of the house, whether she is a wife, mother, or grandmother.

And the eclipse of the sun in a dream may indicate the death or separation of the wife or the absence of the guardian of grace.

Also, seeing dust covering the sun in a dream, or clouds obscuring the sun's rays in a dream, may indicate illness and concerns for one of the parents or one of those with authority.

And the veil of the sun in a dream with clouds of smoke and dust may also indicate that the reality is hidden from the seer and his need to scrutinize matters, and Allah knows best.

Seeing the veil of the sun in a dream for someone who is sick or who has a sick person is not good in it, and it may indicate the approaching life of the patient and his death unless the sleeper sees that the sun appears after the veil and he is sick; This indicates that he woke up from his illness, and Allah is the Healer.

Interpretation of seeing the black sun in a dream

Ibn Sirin adds that the darkness of the sun in a dream if it is not due to an eclipse or one of the reasons we mentioned; indicates the oppression of the ruler and the ruler, as the black sun in a dream without an eclipse indicates the father's wrongdoing against his children, and the misguidance and oppression of the master of the house.

Al-Nabulsi says that seeing the sun as red in a dream as if its color is the color of blood; It has a bad indication, so the red sun in a dream indicates illness, unemployment, and depression, or it indicates the death of the son of the dreamer.

Seeing the sun falling from the sky in a dream

The fall of the sun from the sky in a dream indicates the death of the ruler or the sultan, or those who are attributed to the sun, whom we referred to earlier.

Seeing the sun falling into the sea in a dream may indicate the death of the father or mother, or the approaching life of the one who has direct authority over the seer, such as his manager or teacher.

Likewise, whoever sees a bird swallowing the sun in a dream, or sees the sun burning in a dream; His dream indicated the death of the ruler of that land or the death of one of his parents; Allah knows the ages.

As for the one who sees the sun descending in his house without harm, this indicates the return of the traveller or the strength and enjoyment of power over the people of the house or the common people.

There is no good in seeing the sun on the bed of the seer because it indicates hot diseases and fever that make him sleep in his bed.

Interpretation of holding the sun in a dream

And whoever said, "I saw that I held the sun in my hand in a dream," his vision indicates his firmness in his authority and his ability to achieve glory and honour if he is one of its people. But if the sultan did not meet him and saw that he was holding the sun by his hand, or he saw the sun in his lap in a dream; His dreams indicate the return of an absent person or the arrival of a guest on him who will be an important person.

And holding the sun in a dream if the seer's wife is pregnant indicates a child who will dominate his people.

As for the one who catches the black sun in a dream; the ruler calls him to him and takes advice from him or assigns him a high commission. Al-Nabulsi says that seeing the clinging to the sun in a dream denotes the goodness of the people of power and influence.

Seeing more than one sun in a dream, and the sun and the moon meeting together

Concerning seeing more than one sun in a dream, Ibn Sirin says that seeing two suns in a dream may indicate a war between two rulers or a dispute between those in power who were mentioned above. The dream is for the sick, or for those whose intention was to cover up and keep a secret.

And a large number of suns in a dream may also indicate heresies and a large number of interpretations. If their light is moderate and there is no harm from them, it indicates the consensus of opinions. But if the many suns in a dream are so bright and luminous that they dazzle the eyes, this indicates the loss of opinion and the scattering of people.

The meeting of the moon and the sun in a dream indicates an auspicious marriage to a woman of honour, dignity, and beauty, just as the meeting of the sun and moon in a dream indicates the consent of the parents, and Allah Almighty knows best.

Interpretation of seeing the sun in a dream for a married woman

The shining sun in a dream for a married woman indicates her honour in her husband's house, and that she sees good days with her husband, and as for the one who saw her husband fleeing from the sun in a dream, he is fleeing from her, or fleeing from the Sultan's harm.

And the absence of the sun in a dream for a married woman may indicate her husband's absence from her due to travel, death, or divorce, according to the evidence of the dream. Or her husband has a high status, or she bears a son who is a master in his family, and Allah knows best.

Interpretation of seeing the sun in a dream for single women

Seeing the sun in a dream for a single woman may indicate her marriage to a man who has an affair among his people or who has authority and influence over the common people, and there is no good in seeing the sunrise from the vagina in the dream for the single because it indicates adultery, as well as for the married woman, according to the interpretation of Ibn Sirin.

And the rising of the sun in the house for the single person also indicates her marriage to a well-off man who cherishes her and who has a livelihood from him, and as for the one who saw the sun setting in a dream, this may indicate the death of her father, or the absence of the sun in a dream indicates to the single woman that the end of something she is in is near, whether it is good or evil. And there is no good in seeing sunburns in a dream for a single woman because it indicates torment in love.

Interpretation of seeing the sun in a dream for a pregnant woman

The rising of the sun in a dream for the pregnant woman indicates her safe birth, and whoever saw that she gave birth to the sun in a dream, her son was a master of his people. As for seeing the absence of the sun in a dream for the pregnant woman, there is no good in it and may indicate the death of the fetus, according to the interpretation of Ibn Sirin, and Allah knows best.

cases of seeing the sun in a dream

Fleeing from the sun's heat in a dream to the shade indicates deliverance from danger and worry, and escaping from the shade to the sun in a dream with the intention of warming, indicates the dreamer's escape from need and issues and ease in his financial affairs.

Swallowing the sun in a dream has no good in it, according to Ibn Sirin, and whoever sees that he swallows the sun in a dream; life will be disturbed and will be distressed.

Struggling with the sun in a dream or quarrelling with it may indicate that the seer is rebelling against authority, which may be the authority of the ruler or the authority of the father, or the authority of the husband for the woman.

Whoever saw the sun splitting in a dream or seeing the splitting of the sun in a dream; indicates a dispute between the king and his minister or one of his army commanders, and the fate of the conflict between them will be like the condition of the sun after its splitting. If the sun splits, then every part of it becomes the sun; the dissenter from the ruler became the ruler himself and the equal of his master.

Other cases of seeing the sun in a dream

And that the explosion of the sun in a dream indicates an accident that will happen to the common people and indicates that we are at the end of time; Allah knows.

Whoever sees the sun talking to him in a dream will be honoured and elevated by the sultan. As for catching up with the sun in a dream, it indicates captivity and imprisonment with a great man.

And whoever sees that he turns into the sun in a dream becomes a sultan, a king, or an important person in his people or his profession according to his condition, and he will be able to do all of that according to his rays in the dream, or he will have an achievement that people can benefit from.

Sitting in the sun's rays in a dream without harm indicates benefit from a person with authority and influence.

Sunburn in a dream is not good and indicates the torment of the sultan or a great scandal, and sunburn in a dream may indicate the torment of passion and love.

The damage that the sun causes in a dream, if it is to the seer, in particular, indicates harm to his family and loved ones or his livelihood, and if it is general harm, such as seeing the sunburn plants and orchards and so on; Indicate epidemics, famine, and drought.

Fear and pain, however, are like the ebb, which withdraws that which was gathered. For fear and terror render the face pale and the countenance bleak and hideous by withdrawing the blood and the spirits, and cause melancholy to corrupt the little blood which remains in the veins, and fills the imagination with frightful dreams. It is necessary, therefore, that the accents with which we express the different affections and passions of the soul be different, and that some of them imitate and represent the flow of spirits and blood, and others the ebb, that the former be quick, lively, cheerful, and similar to the flowers and odors of spring, and the latter be similar to rain, snow, winter, and all that is disagreeable, that the former be similar to consonances and ensemble pieces, and the latter to dissonances and disturbing noises, and finally, that the former have as many perfections as the latter have imperfections.
We must see whether it is possible to establish four principal accents according to these four different passions. For the accents of which we speak here can be called the word or discourse of the passions, just as words and ordinary discourse are called the discourse of the mind, which partakes more of artificial means than of nature, just as that of the passions partakes more of nature than of artificial means. Consequently, the latter is less subject to concealment than the former. With regard to the accent of joy, it is certain that it is different from that of sorrow. That of joy, however, includes that of desire and love, just as the triangle includes two right angles, and just as the rational soul includes the sensitive and the vegetative. This accent is cheerful, pleasant, and quite agreeable, and can be divided into as many other accents as there are different degrees of joy and love.
The accent of sorrow is slow, gloomy, and troublesome. That of hatred is more violent, and approaches that of indignation, which is contained in that of choler. With regard to the accent of flight, it is related to that of fear, and that of desire is like that of hope. The accent of despair follows that of sorrow, just as that of boldness follows that of hope and desire. It is difficult, however, to express all these accents." [IV, vi, 13]

Uncovering the Unconscious: Symbolism in Surrealism and Freud's PsychoanalysisFreud's theories of the unconscious mind revolved around dream interpretation, the Oedipal complex, and the roles of the id, ego, and superego. He believed that dream images, symbols, and metaphors were a direct expression of the unconscious mind. Through his meticulous study of dream symbols and their meanings, Freud made a connection between an individual's unconscious desires and the symbols in the artwork of Surrealism.

One of the most recognizable symbols used in Surrealism is the use of the female body. The female body represents a myriad of things, such as fertility, beauty, and sexuality. In Surrealism, the female body symbolizes the unconscious, as it is a gateway to the unknown. The female body also serves as a representation of the innermost desires of the subconscious mind.

A key element of this movement is the use of clocks and the concept of time. Clocks symbolically represent surrealism's commitment to expanding and deconstructing the notion of reality. They challenge the idea that time is linear and represent the movement's commitment to creating something unique and unpredictable. In art projects and literature, clocks often appear as a device to express surrealist themes and ideas. By exploring the link between clocks and surrealism, we gain a deeper understanding of the movement and its legacy.

Sigmund Freud had a lot to say about surrealism and the concept of time. He believed that time was an essential element in understanding the unconscious mind and that it was important to break away from traditional conceptions of time in order to explore our subconscious. Freud also believed that surrealism was an expression of the unconscious and that clocks, and the idea of time, play a crucial role in this exploration. He argued that clocks are symbolic of surrealism's commitment to free-association and breaking away from traditional conceptions of reality. Freud's ideas helped to shape our understanding of surrealism and its relationship to the concept of time.

Another prominent symbol used in Surrealism is the image of the sun. The sun is a powerful symbol of energy, power, and enlightenment. In Surrealism, the sun is used to represent the inner energy of the unconscious mind. By using the sun as a symbol, Surrealists were able to convey the power of the unconscious and its potential for awakening the mind.

In addition to the female body and the sun, Surrealists often used other symbols to represent the unconscious. One common example is the apple, which symbolizes knowledge, temptation, and the power of the unconscious. The apple can represent the forbidden knowledge that lies within the depths of the unconscious, offering insight into the hidden desires of the mind. The apple also symbolizes temptation, as it calls to the viewer to indulge in the secrets of the unconscious. Through the use of the apple, Surrealists were able to express the power of the unconscious and its influence on the mind.

Finally, the use of automatism is another important element of Surrealism. Automatism is the process of letting the subconscious take over, allowing for the expression of innermost thoughts and desires without judgement. Through the use of automatism, Surrealists were able to create art that truly embodied the spirit of the unconscious.

In conclusion, the link between symbolism in Surrealism and Freud's theories of the unconscious is clear. Through the use of symbols, Surrealists were able to express their innermost desires and unlock the secrets of their subconscious. Freud's theories provided an insight into the power of dream symbolism and the role of the unconscious in creating art. Together, Freud and the Surrealists revolutionized the way we think about art and the subconscious.

According to psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud, the manifest content of a dream includes the actual images, thoughts and content contained within the dream. The manifest content is the elements of the dream that we remember upon awakening.

In his book The Interpretation of Dreams, Sigmund Freud suggested that the content of dreams is related to wish fulfillment. Freud believed that the manifest content of a dream, or the actual imagery and events of the dream, served to disguise the latent content, or the unconscious wishes of the dreamer.1

The journey from womb to dreamland marks the remarkable passage from prenatal existence to the mysterious realm of dreams. This transformative odyssey begins in the protective cocoon of the womb, where the seeds of consciousness are sown. As a fetus floats in the amniotic embrace, the first inklings of sensory experience lay the foundation for a future voyage into the world of dreams. The symphony of sounds and sensations:

In the womb, a symphony of sounds and sensations becomes the prenatal soundtrack of existence. The rhythmic heartbeat of the mother, the gentle lull of amniotic fluid, and the muffled echoes of the external world create a sensory tapestry. These early stimuli, though perceived in utero, play a crucial role in shaping the neural architecture that will later process the kaleidoscope of dreams.

Prenatal bliss: Navigating the intrauterine landscape:

Prenatal bliss is an ethereal experience, a state of pure existence unencumbered by the complexities of the external world. Within the womb's sanctuary, the developing fetus navigates an intrauterine landscape, floating weightlessly in a liquid embrace. This idyllic existence fosters a sense of security, laying the groundwork for the peaceful transition to dreamland.

The gateway to dreamland: Sleep in the womb:

As the fetus slumbers in the womb, sleep becomes a precursor to the nocturnal adventures awaiting in the realm of dreams. Studies suggest that fetuses experience periods of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, indicative of the early stages of dream-like brain activity. This prenatal slumber serves as the gateway to the subconscious, where the foundations of imagination and creativity are laid.

Beyond the womb: Navigating the dreamscape:

The transition from womb to dreamland is a continuum, extending beyond the confines of prenatal existence. Infants, upon entering the world, bring with them the imprint of their prenatal experiences. As they embark on the journey of life, the neural pathways forged in the womb continue to shape their dreamscape. Early childhood, with its vivid imagination and fantastical dreams, reflects the seamless connection between prenatal bliss and the evolving landscape of dreams.

From the serene sanctuary of the womb to the boundless landscapes of dreamland, the journey is a tapestry woven with the threads of sensory experiences, prenatal bliss, and the perpetual dance between consciousness and dreams.

Enchantment of the Unseen: The Symbolism of Magic in Dreams

Magic in dreams symbolizes our desire for wonder, the power of transformation, and the allure of the unknown. These dreams reflect our aspirations for change, the challenges of embracing the mysterious, and the opportunities for growth and understanding through the exploration of magical realms. The imagery of a mystical figure casting a spell, surrounded by swirling magical energy and symbols, evokes a sense of enchantment, the mystery of magical forces at work, and the thrill of venturing into uncharted territories. Dreams of magic illustrate our fears, aspirations, and the pursuit of understanding and embracing the transformative power of our imagination.

Introduction

Dreams featuring magic delve into themes of wonder, transformation, and the exploration of the unknown, serving as metaphors for our innermost desires for change, the enchantment of the mysterious, and the journey towards discovering and harnessing the transformative power within us. These visions invite us to consider the role of magic as a symbol of our capacity for imagination, creativity, and the embracing of possibilities beyond the ordinary confines of reality.

Symbolic Meanings of Magic in Dreams

Wonder and Enchantment: Magic represents the sense of wonder and enchantment we seek in life, emphasizing the beauty and awe of experiencing the world through a lens of curiosity and openness to the extraordinary.

Transformation and Change: It symbolizes the power of transformation and change, reflecting our desire for personal growth, the shedding of old ways, and the embracing of new possibilities and identities.

The Unknown and Exploration: Dreams of magic underscore our fascination with the unknown and the thrill of exploration, highlighting our journey towards understanding the mysteries of life and the depths of our own psyche.

Psychological Perspective on Magic in Dreams

Psychologically, magic in dreams can mirror our subconscious yearnings for wonder and transformation, our attitudes towards the mysterious and the unexplained, and our intrinsic need for creativity and imagination. They may indicate our inner conflicts, aspirations for self-discovery, and the emotional and psychological engagement with the concept of magic as a metaphor for the unseen forces and potential within and around us.

Cultural Interpretations of Dreaming About Magic

Culturally, magic is often associated with folklore, mythology, and the storytelling traditions of various societies, symbolizing the collective imagination, the role of supernatural beliefs in shaping cultural identities, and the personal significance of magical narratives in inspiring wonder, caution, and insight into the human condition.

Spiritual Meanings of Magic in Dreams

Spiritually, magic in dreams might signify the connection with the divine or the mystical, the quest for spiritual awakening, and the pursuit of higher knowledge and understanding through the exploration of esoteric and occult practices. They can represent the spiritual journey of tapping into unseen energies, the power of intention and manifestation, and the exploration of the boundaries between the physical and the metaphysical.

How to Interpret Your Magic Dreams

Examine the Magic's Nature: The nature of the magic—its effects, purpose, source—can offer insights into your desires for transformation, your feelings about the unknown, and your perceptions of the power and potential within you and the world.

Consider the Context: The context in which the magic occurs—solitary practice, a shared experience, a challenge—can shed light on your relationship with wonder and change, your interactions with the mysterious, and your journey towards embracing and harnessing the transformative aspects of life.

Reflect on Your Emotions: Your emotional response to the magic in the dream can reveal your subconscious feelings about the possibilities for change, your fears and aspirations regarding the unknown, and your longing for a life filled with wonder, creativity, and the exploration of the boundless potential of the imagination.

Interpretation of seeing stars in a dream

The stars and planets have always been likened to scholars, jurists, and righteous people, and the Messenger, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, likened his companions to stars, and Joseph, peace be upon him, saw his parents and brothers as the sun, moon, and planets, as the interpretation of seeing stars in a dream depends on this similarity to a large extent, and the context of the dream and the details of the vision and its evidence remains the decisive factor in the interpretation.

The general meaning of seeing stars in a dream

Muhammad Ibn Sirin says in his book "Munkhab al-Kalam fi Tafsir al-Ahlam" that the stars in a dream are indicative of people, so the names of the stars are known; The masculine ones indicate males and the feminine ones indicate females, and the stars that are guided by indicate the companions of the Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, because he said, "My companions are like stars." They also indicate scholars and jurists.

Interpretation of looking at the stars in a dream

It indicates sitting with a scholar or a worshiper and seeing the stars shining in the sky or seeing the twinkling stars denotes sitting with scholars with different specializations and broad knowledge.

And if the light of the stars is dazzling in the dream, it indicates a scientist who comes up with a theory or explains an idea, while seeing the stars extinguished in a dream indicates a reduction in enjoining good and forbidding evil and seeing dim stars in a dream is the silence of the scholars.

And looking at the stars during the day may indicate a vision that calls for guidance and righteousness, and if seeing the stars in a clear sky indicates the security of people, and as for seeing them in a cloudy sky, then people fear the authority and fear of scholars, and whoever sees the stars making a shape in the sky, then this is a union of scholars or a bond or a charity.

And seeing the counting and counting of the stars in a dream indicates that good people are counted among the people, and the movement of the stars conveys goodness, and seeing the stars surrounding the moon indicates that the nation is following the approach of the final Prophet, peace and blessings are upon him, and whoever sees as if the stars are fighting in the sky, then the imams of the people differ, and God knows best.

Looking at the stars in a dream is interpreted based on what the sleeper sees in detail about the conditions and movement of the stars, as Ibn Sirin says that seeing the stars and moons in a state of struggle and fighting, for example, indicates war and battles between kings and ministers.

He saw the stars fighting and he had two wives or partners, so this may indicate their fighting and rivalry, and whoever sees in a dream that he is looking at the star and following it, then he follows the Sunnah of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his companions.

As for seeing the stars during the day, it indicates the disclosure of the hidden and the disclosure of matters, and it may indicate calamities according to the interpretation of Ibn Sirin, and this will be according to the abundance and clarity of the stars in the dream.

As for whoever sees the stars in his house together; If the stars are shining in the house, the best people gather in it for joy and happiness, and if the stars are without rays or light, then the gathering of people in the house of the seer is a disaster, and seeing the stars under a roof is not good in general.

Falling stars in a dream and dreaming of catching a star

Ibn Sirin says that the interpretation of the falling stars in a dream indicates death in the place, so seeing a star falling into the sea or seeing a bird catching a star from the sky indicates death or a lot of killing as much as the sleeper sees of the falling stars, even if the falling star from the sky is known. In his name, it indicates death that occurs in one sex and not another.

If it is masculine, it occurs among males, and if it is feminine, killing occurs among females, and God knows best.

And seeing the star falling in the lap of the seer indicates the attainment of power and elevation for those who are worthy of it, and likewise seeing the grasping of the stars in a dream or controlling them.

As for seeing the stars falling from the sky on the head, if the seer is in debt, the creditor will demand it, and if the one who fell on his head is ill, then his term has come close, and the same is for those who picked up the stars from the earth, and as for whoever sees the stars falling on him from the sky or catches them and he is absent on travel or The like, the absence will return to him, and God knows best.

And theft of the star from the sky indicates that the seer is stealing something from a king or a ruler, and reaching out to the sky and taking the stars in a dream also indicates attaining high positions.

Seeing falling stars in a dream

The interpretation of the falling stars in a dream in general is that it indicates the death of the best of people, so whoever sees a big star falling to the ground may indicate the death of a scholar in that country, and seeing the stars falling from the sky like rain may indicate a large number of martyrs, and whoever sees the stars falling and causing destruction, that is anger God and the approach of the true promise, and God knows best.

As for seeing the stars falling in the house, this indicates that the people of the house learned useful sciences, and whoever sees the stars rising from the earth to the sky, this is the height of trust and honesty from people.

And he moves it and becomes the owner of power.

Interpretation of seeing stars in a dream for a woman

Ibn Sirin says that a woman's vision of the stars fighting in the sky may indicate a quarrel over her husband and another man, a quarrel between her children, or enmity and a rivalry between her son and her husband.

To give birth to a male child, and the newborn has a status unless the pregnant woman sees in a dream that the star is feminine and gives birth to a female, and her luck of beauty and brightness is as much as the star has good and reputation.

Other cases of seeing stars in a dream

Ibn Sirin says that the stars or planets that were known to be worshiped instead of God indicate their vision in a dream of men or women who have no good in them or their religion.

And the meeting of planets and luminous stars in a dream for those who are on a journey indicates goodness, God willing.

Ibn Sirin adds that seeing eating stars in a dream indicates that the seer or the one who was eating the star in the dream; eats people's money, and as for whoever sees that he is absorbing planets or stars in a dream, he will benefit from knowledge from the people of knowledge.

And that seeing the stars in a dream for the rich is an increase in righteousness, and the meeting of religion and the world for him, and for the poor, sustenance from a ruler or a scholar, and the stars in a dream for the believer are promotion, elevation, and an increase in righteousness, and for the disobedient, repentance at the hands of a scholar and response to the advice, and the stars for the prisoner, relief, and for the sad or distressed, relief from God, and for whom He was taking precedence over the matter of doing it and raising it, so seeing the stars after istikharah is good and abundant, and God knows best.

The Interpretation of Dreams (German: Die Traumdeutung) is an 1899 book by Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis, in which the author introduces his theory of the unconscious with respect to dream interpretation, and discusses what would later become the theory of the Oedipus complex. Freud revised the book at least eight times and, in the third edition, added an extensive section which treated dream symbolism very literally, following the influence of Wilhelm Stekel. Freud said of this work, "Insight such as this falls to one's lot but once in a lifetime."

Dated 1900, the book was first published in an edition of 600 copies, which did not sell out for eight years. The Interpretation of Dreams later gained in popularity, and seven more editions were published in Freud's lifetime.

Because of the book's length and complexity, Freud also wrote an abridged version called On Dreams. The original text is widely regarded as one of Freud's most significant works.

Certain constitutions identify the foundations for happiness and well-being, alluding to subjects such as agriculture, health, environmental quality, and the entitlement to land. Article 4 of the Mexican Constitution of 1917 identifies "the right to a healthy environment" as essential for any person's "own development and well-being."Footnote 65 Article 366 of the Colombian Constitution of 1991 ordains that "[t]he general well-being and improvement of the population's quality of life are social purposes of the State" and the "objective of their activity [is] . . . to address the unfulfilled public health, educational, environmental, and drinking water needs of those affected."Footnote 66 Article 57 of the Costa Rican Constitution of 1949 guarantees the workers' right "to a minimum salary, fixed periodically, for a normal working day, that procures them well-being and dignified existence."Footnote 67 Article 247 of the Haitian Constitution of 1987 identifies "[a]griculture, which is the main source of the Nation's wealth" as "a guarantee of the well-being of the people and the socio-economic progress of the Nation."Footnote 68 Article 109 of the Constitution of Mozambique of 2004 provides that "[a]s a universal means for the creation of wealth and of social well-being, the use and enjoyment of land shall be the right of all the Mozambican people."Footnote 69
One common pillar of happiness resides within the realm of work and labor, under which the meaningful involvement in and fulfillment derived from work play a pivotal role in enhancing overall well-being. Article 21 of the Guyana Constitution of 1980 considers that "[t]he source of the growth of social wealth and of the well-being of the people, and of each individual, is the labour of the people."Footnote 70 Article 35 of the Azerbaijani Constitution identifies that "[w]ork is the basis of individual and social well-being."Footnote 71 Article 25 of the Tanzanian Constitution of 1977 goes even further and expresses that "[w]ork alone creates the material wealth in society, and is the source of the well-being of the people and the measure of human dignity."Footnote 72
Despite having ventured into the foundations of happiness, many happiness provisions still fall short of capably articulating an explicit constitutional meaning for the two remain conceptually distinct. The murkiness may furthermore be attributed to the fact that some drafters or interpreters are simply not bothered, for they consider happiness provisions as mere "window dressing"Footnote 73 vacuous rhetoric the single function of which is to coat a veneer of legitimacy on the state without any intended substantive or legal impact.

Born out of the ashes of World War I, Surrealism emerged as a revolutionary artistic movement that sought to challenge the boundaries of perception and unlock the mysteries of the human psyche. Join us as we delve into the surreal landscapes of dreams and delve into the captivating world of Surrealist art.

The Birth of Surrealism: A Rebellion Against Rationalism

In the aftermath of the Great War, Europe found itself gripped by a profound sense of disillusionment and existential angst. It was against this backdrop of social upheaval and cultural upheaval that Surrealism was born. Led by the enigmatic figure of André Breton, Surrealist artists sought to liberate the creative impulse from the shackles of rationality and embrace the irrational, the subconscious, and the absurd. Rejecting the constraints of conventional artistic techniques, they embarked on a quest to explore the hidden recesses of the mind and give form to the ineffable.

Exploring the Unconscious: The Art of Surrealist Manifestations

At the heart of Surrealism lies a fascination with the unconscious mind and its capacity to conjure forth images of profound beauty and strangeness. Surrealist artists such as Salvador Dalí, René Magritte, and Max Ernst employed a variety of techniques, including automatism, dream analysis, and juxtaposition, to unlock the secrets of the subconscious and give shape to their innermost fantasies and fears. The result was a rich and diverse body of work characterized by its dreamlike imagery, bizarre juxtapositions, and haunting symbolism.

The Legacy of Surrealism: A Source of Inspiration and Provocation

Though Surrealism may have reached its zenith in the early 20th century, its legacy continues to resonate in the art world to this day. From the uncanny photomontages of contemporary artists like Cindy Sherman to the mind-bending digital creations of the digital age, Surrealism has left an indelible mark on the collective imagination. Its influence can be seen not only in the realm of visual art but also in literature, film, fashion, and popular culture, where its spirit of rebellion and experimentation continues to inspire new generations of artists and thinkers.

Surrealism as a Gateway to the Unconscious

In conclusion, Surrealism stands as a testament to the boundless power of the imagination to transcend the constraints of reality and explore the mysteries of the human psyche. Through its daring exploration of the unconscious mind, Surrealism invites us to embrace the irrational, the absurd, and the fantastical—to journey into the depths of our own subconscious and confront the hidden truths that lie within. In a world increasingly dominated by rationality and reason, Surrealism serves as a reminder of the importance of embracing the irrational and the mysterious—to venture into the unknown and discover new realms of possibility.

Whispers of the Night

In the heart of a verdant forest, where the trees whispered ancient secrets and the wind sang melodies of old, there existed a tribe known for their profound connection with the dream realm. They were the guardians of dreams, skilled weavers of hopes and protectors against the night's darker tides. Central to their mystical practices was the Dreamcatcher, a sacred artifact of unparalleled beauty and power, crafted not merely by hands but by hearts intertwined with the very essence of nature and spirit.

The creation of a Dreamcatcher was a rite, passed down through generations, enveloping not just the craft but the lore of its purpose. Fashioned from the willow's gentle boughs, it formed a circle representing the cycle of life, with threads as delicate as spider's silk woven into a web, a mirror to the weavings of fate. At its heart hung feathers and beads, each a story, a memory, a wish.

Legend held that the Dreamcatcher was birthed from the love of a spider, a creature of remarkable skill and patience. In the earliest days, when the world was young and night brought fear to the hearts of the children, a spider listened to the worries of the tribe. Moved by their plight, it spun a web of silver light, capturing the moon's gentle glow. "This," it said, "will be your shield against the night's despair, a catcher of dreams. Let only the good dreams pass, sliding down the feathers to the sleeping ones below. The nightmares shall be entangled, dissolved by the first light of dawn."

As centuries unfolded, the Dreamcatcher found its way into the lore of many, a symbol of protection, hope, and the sacred bond between the Earth and its children. It taught them the power of good intentions, the strength found in unity with nature, and the importance of guarding one's spirit against the shadows.

But beyond its tangible form, the Dreamcatcher whispered a deeper truth – that every soul is interwoven in the great tapestry of existence, each thread a story, each knot a lesson. It served as a reminder that while nightmares may come, the strength to overcome them lies within, bolstered by the love and support of the community and the ancient wisdom that guides them.

So in the quiet of the night, under the watchful gaze of the stars, the Dreamcatcher sways gently, a guardian of sleep, a bearer of dreams. And the tribe, nestled in the embrace of the forest, sleeps peacefully, their dreams guided through the night by the loving hands of their ancestors, woven into the legacy of the Dreamcatcher.

Gross National Happiness (GNH) is an indicator developed in Bhutan in the Himalayas, based on the concept elaborated in 1972 by the then King Jigme Singye Wangchuck. GNH is based on the premise that the calculation of "wealth" should consider other aspects besides economic development: the preservation of the environment and the quality of life of the people. The goal of a society should be the integration of material development with psychological, cultural, and spiritual aspects - all in harmony with the Earth.

In the quiet corners of the night, when the world rests under the cloak of darkness, I find myself wandering through the tapestry of dreams. It is a realm where reality intertwines with the surreal, where the ordinary becomes extraordinary, and the boundaries of possibility stretch like threads across the loom of imagination.

Each night, as I surrender to the embrace of sleep, the loom of dreams weaves its intricate patterns. Dreams, like vibrant threads of silk, entwine with the fibers of my subconscious, creating a tapestry that unfolds in the theater of my mind.

In this ethereal space, I become a spectator and a participant, a traveler navigating the landscapes of the fantastical. Dreams unfurl like kaleidoscopic vistas, painting the canvas of my mind with scenes that defy the constraints of time and space. I dance with the impossible, my every step leaving footprints on the soft fabric of reverie.

There are dreams that linger like a delicate fragrance, elusive and ephemeral. They are the whispers of the subconscious, carrying fragments of forgotten memories and unspoken desires. In this tapestry of dreams, the past and the future converge in a dance of shadows and light, and I become a curator of the fleeting moments that slip through the hourglass of slumber.

Some dreams are like riddles, their meanings hidden beneath layers of symbolism and metaphor. They beckon me to decipher their enigmatic language, inviting me to explore the depths of my own psyche. Each symbol, a brushstroke on the canvas, adds to the richness of the tapestry, a visual symphony that resonates with the chords of the unconscious.

And then, there are the dreams that defy reason, soaring into realms of pure fantasy. In these flights of fancy, I become a voyager exploring uncharted territories, encountering mythical creatures, and embracing the magic that resides in the folds of the dream-weaved fabric.

As I navigate the tapestry of dreams, I am reminded that this nocturnal realm is a sanctuary of the soul. Here, the constraints of reality loosen their grip, and the boundaries between the conceivable and the fantastical blur into a harmonious blend of possibilities. The tapestry of dreams is a reflection of the boundless potential that resides within the human spirit, an ever-unfolding narrative that transcends the waking world.

And so, each night, I surrender to the loom of dreams, allowing it to craft a new chapter in the ever-evolving tapestry of my nocturnal adventures. In the quiet hours before dawn, I wake with the residue of dreams clinging to my consciousness, grateful for the journey through this surreal landscape, a journey that enriches the fabric of my waking life with the vibrant hues of imagination and wonder.

Icebergs in dreams symbolize our hidden depths, the vastness of the unconscious mind, and the aspects of ourselves or our lives that remain unseen or unexplored. These dreams reflect our inner mysteries, the complexities of our psyche, and the opportunities for growth and understanding through the exploration of the hidden and the unseen. The imagery of a massive iceberg, with a significant portion submerged underwater, evokes awe, the mystery of the unknown, and the potential for discovery, illustrating how dreams of icebergs can reflect our fears, aspirations, and the pursuit of understanding and embracing the submerged aspects of our personalities and experiences.

Introduction

Psychologically, icebergs in dreams can mirror our feelings about the unexplored aspects of our personality, our curiosity or fear of the unknown, and our subconscious yearning for deeper self-understanding. They may indicate our readiness or reluctance to delve into the unconscious mind and confront the hidden elements of our psyche.

Culturally, icebergs are often associated with mystery, danger, and the unseen, symbolizing the human fascination with and fear of the unknown. How to Interpret Your Iceberg Dreams

Examine the Visibility: The portion of the iceberg visible above water compared to what is submerged can offer insights into the balance between your conscious awareness and the unconscious mind, highlighting the areas of your life or psyche that may require deeper exploration.

Consider the Context: The context in which the iceberg appears—peaceful, threatening, melting—can shed light on your feelings towards the hidden aspects of yourself, your readiness to explore the unknown, and the potential changes or revelations you may be facing.

Reflect on Your Emotions: Your emotional response to the iceberg in the dream can reveal your subconscious feelings about the mysteries and challenges of self-discovery, your fears or excitement about what lies beneath the surface, and your desire for deeper understanding and personal growth.

More of Sigmund Freud's thoughts on dreams

Ego – concerned with the conscious, the rational, the moral and the self-aware aspect of the mind.

Superego – the censor for the id, which is also responsible for enforcing the moral codes of the ego.

When you are awake, the impulses and desires of the id are suppressed by the superego. Through dreams, you are able to get a glimpse into your unconscious or the id. Because your guards are down during the dream state, your unconscious has the opportunity to act out and express the hidden desires of the id. However, the desires of the id can, at times, be so disturbing and even psychologically harmful that a "censor" comes into play and translates the id's disturbing content into a more acceptable symbolic form. This helps to preserve sleep and prevent you from waking up shocked at the images. As a result, confusing and cryptic dream images occur.

According to Freud, the reason you struggle to remember your dreams, is because the superego is at work. It is doing its job by protecting the conscious mind from the disturbing images and desires conjured by the unconscious."

The meaning of the dream symbol: Dew

Generally speaking the symbolism of dew is closely akin to that of rain, but its influence is of a more subtle order. 'The waters which spring from the heart,' wrote Callixtus II Xanthopoulos, 'fill the entire inner being with divine dew.' 'The pearly dew of the noble godhead' of which Angelus Silesius writes has a similar significance, but suggests the redeeming blood of Christ. Now, in medieval iconography, the blood, which falls drop by drop from the Centurion's spear, is also the heavenly dew, the symbol of redemption and rebirth, which recurs in Hermetic writings and also in the Jewish Kabbalah, where it is an emanation of the Tree of Life. Apparently there was a 'tree of sweet dew' on Mount Kun-Lun, the Chinese centre of the Earth.

Photo Gallery:

Pliny calls dew 'the sweat of Heaven, the spittle of the stars'. In Indian sacred scriptures it is 'the symbol of the word of God'. Dew is a symbol of regeneration.

If the heavenly dew of the Jews restored life to dry bones, the lunar dew of the Chinese cleared the vision and allowed the attainment of immortality. The Immortals on the island of Ho-chu feed upon air and dew, according to Lao-Tzu. The dew is drawn from the Moon in a huge shell (to kiue). It was gathered by such mortals as the Han Emperor, Wu, in a jade chalice, to be mixed with powdered jade.

In China, too, dew was associated with the princely power of the yang, sometimes in opposition to the yin influence of rain. The down-dropping of 'gentle dew', according to Lao-Tzu (ch. 32), is the sign of the peaceful marriage of Heaven and Earth. Dew is also born of a perfect harmony struck on a four-stringed lute.

On the other hand, in Buddhist terms, the 'world of dew' is that of appearances, and is a sign of the ephemeral nature of material things and of the brevity of life.

The Old Greeks related dew with fertility myths, dionysos embodying the fertilizing dew of Heaven. Texts from Ras Shamrah place Astarte in contact with the sea as with a fertilizing dew, and the same is true of aphrodite. It should be emphasized that these are love-gods and goddesses.

The importance of dew in so many rituals and magic spells arises from the fact that it resolves the confrontation between the upper and the lower, the heavenly and the terrestrial waters. Dew is pure water, precious water, pre-eminently primeval water, a distillation of the generative powers of the watery principle. The Fon of Dahomey (now Benin) call it 'Mother-Water' and in the Voodoo pantheon, the deified watery element materializes in the shape of drops of dew preserved in a calabash. In Bambara mythology the primal waters first appeared on Earth in the shape of dew. The spider, the Ashanti Demiurge, first created the Sun, Moon and stars and divided night from day and next created dew, Harry Tegnaeus concluding: 'thus this concept of dew should be related to that of vegetation and fertility.'

Similarly North American Indians believed that 'The Great Dew Eagle' regenerated the soil blasted by evil spirits.

Walking through the French Quarter, one can easily imagine the city's past, when pirates and buccaneers roamed its streets, and the echoes of their footsteps resonate in the cobblestones beneath your feet.

The Rhythmic Pulse of Jazz

New Orleans is the birthplace of jazz, and the city's musical heritage is palpable in every corner. From the legendary Preservation Hall to the smoky dive bars on Frenchmen Street, the waking and dreaming of New Orleans find their most vivid expression in music. The soulful melodies of jazz, with their improvisational spirit, speak to the city's dynamic energy, its ability to embrace the unexpected, and its relentless pursuit of joy.

The Haunted Embrace of the Cemeteries

New Orleans' cemeteries, unlike any other, are above ground, sprawling gardens of ornate mausoleums and family tombs. These cemeteries are not places of sorrow but rather a unique part of the city's fabric, where the waking and dreaming become intertwined. They are places of beauty, where the dead are given a place of honor, and where the living come to pay their respects, to reflect on the cycles of life and death. The stories whispered among the tombs, the legends of voodoo, and the hauntings that are said to linger in the cemeteries all contribute to the city's eerie, almost otherworldly aura.

The Culinary Delights of New Orleans

Food is an integral part of the waking and dreaming experience in New Orleans. From the rich and flavorful gumbo to the spicy and soul-satisfying jambalaya, the city's cuisine is a reflection of its diverse cultural heritage. The aromas of Creole and Cajun cooking, with their unique blend of African, French, and Spanish influences, fill the air, inviting visitors to indulge in the city's culinary delights.

The Voodoo Queen and the Spirits of the Past

Voodoo is deeply ingrained in the cultural fabric of New Orleans, adding another layer to the city's enigmatic allure. The waking and dreaming are not merely a state of being in New Orleans but a tangible presence, as the city's voodoo traditions weave their way through its history, culture, and everyday life. The city's history is punctuated by the stories of Marie Laveau, the legendary voodoo queen who still holds sway over the hearts and minds of many New Orleanians. Her legacy continues to inspire a sense of the mystical and the unseen, a sense that the spirits of the past are never truly gone, and that the city's soul is a complex and intricate tapestry of the living and the dead.

The Mardi Gras Carnival: A Waking Dream

Mardi Gras, the city's signature celebration, is an explosion of color, music, and revelry. It's a time when the waking and dreaming merge into one, when the city embraces its playful side and throws off the shackles of convention. The parade floats, the costumed revelers, the beads and trinkets, and the infectious energy of the celebration create a temporary reality where anything is possible.

Waking and Dreaming in New Orleans: A Conclusion

New Orleans is a city that defies easy categorization. It is a place where history and modernity collide, where the past and present exist in a dynamic equilibrium, where the waking and dreaming merge into one, creating a unique and intoxicating experience. It's a city that will leave you questioning the boundaries of reality, where the extraordinary seems commonplace, and where the magic of the city unfolds in every corner. Whether it's the soulful melodies of jazz, the eerie whispers of the cemeteries, the intoxicating aromas of Creole cooking, or the vibrant energy of Mardi Gras, New Orleans is a place where the spirit of the city and the spirit of the individual intertwine in an unforgettable and captivating dance.

Activation-Synthesis Theory. The Activation-Synthesis Theory states that dreams are efforts of the brain to make sense of the neural activity that takes place during sleep. According to this theory, dreaming involves internal stimulation, while being awake involves external stimulation. Accordingly, neuroscientists attribute the sudden shifting of dream scenes to the rise and fall of levels of neurotransmitters in the brain. Neuroscientific research also shows that the cerebral cortex activates with different aspects of dreaming, and that the REM stage of sleep leads to odd physical movements, not only of the eyeballs, but also with the rest of the body. Critics of the Activation-Synthesis Theory point to the strong attention it gives on the role of the reticular formation (a part of the brain involved in stereotyped patterns of behavior) in dreaming; and the lack of credit the theory gives to the role of life events in influencing dreams.

Question: Which part of the brain is involved in stereotyped patterns of behavior, according to this theory?
Answer: The reticular formation.

This version of the work uses a rich array of identifiable symbols and visual elements, each carefully selected to guide the viewer through the narrative of the piece.

The inspiration for "Whispers of the Sleeping Sky" arises from the cycles of dreams and wakefulness, where the night brings forth vivid and symbolic narratives offering deep insights, while the day ushers in clarity and conscious activity. This media collage captures the essence of these transitions, portraying the continuous dance between darkness and light, unconscious and conscious states, and the profound interplay between them.

In this media collage, a diverse palette of colors and textures is employed to create a dynamic and immersive visual experience. Symbols of the night—such as stars, crescent moons, and nocturnal creatures—are intertwined with elements of the day, like bright suns, blooming flowers, and awakening birds. Each element serves as a visual metaphor, representing different aspects of the mind's journey through the cycles of rest and wakefulness.

The collage technique allows for a layering of images, where each layer adds depth and complexity to the narrative. Fragmented yet cohesive, the piece invites viewers to piece together the story from the symbols presented, much like interpreting the fragments of a dream upon waking.

"Whispers of the Sleeping Sky" in its media collage form encourages introspection and personal interpretation. The identifiable symbols act as touchpoints for the viewer, providing a framework through which the narrative can be deciphered and understood. The work highlights the fluidity and interconnectedness of the mind's nocturnal and diurnal activities, suggesting that both realms are essential to the human experience.

For me, this media collage represents the harmony between the subconscious whispers of the night and the conscious clarity of the day. It is a visual symphony where each symbol and element plays a part in the grand narrative of the mind's eternal cycle. The process of creating this piece was one of assembling fragments of thought, memory, and imagination, resulting in a tapestry that reflects the complexity and beauty of the human psyche.

"Whispers of the Sleeping Sky" is an invitation to explore the depths of the mind, to embrace the symbols that emerge from our dreams, and to find meaning in the interplay between night and day. Through this work, I hope to inspire viewers to delve into their own inner worlds and discover the narratives that reside within.

Holy Communion, also known as the Eucharist, holds a central place in Christian theology and practice. It is a sacred sacrament that signifies the partaking of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, symbolizing the believer's union with Christ and participation in the divine life. The ritual of Holy Communion is deeply rooted in the Last Supper, a significant event in the life of Jesus Christ, where he shared bread and wine with his disciples, instructing them to partake in remembrance of him.

The act of taking Holy Communion involves the consumption of consecrated bread and wine, which are believed to undergo a spiritual transformation, embodying the presence of Christ. This acceptable symbolic form constituted the manifest dream content, and the technical procedures adopted, particularly that of free association, gave access to the contents of the repressed unconscious, the latent dream content, and herein lay the importance of the dream for Freud.

This is despite the fact that the common lighting strategies are practically focused on energy efficiency or providing the light needed to do the work, or it has been done in the form of a laboratory study under an artificial sky without the presence of humans. Therefore, the current research aims to explain the relationship between daylight and the mental health and happiness of the residents of residential complexes and to increase individual happiness. The current research project is of a causal-comparative type, which through a survey method, describes the correlation between variables in a cross-sectional way in 2013-2014 in short-rise residential complexes (3-7 floors) in the city of Isfahan. To determine the state of happiness, Oxford and Fordyce happiness measurement tool was used. Then the obtained data was analyzed by SPSS software and using descriptive statistics. Data analysis showed that there is a significant difference between the level of happiness of residents of residential complexes and the amount of light in each unit; This means that the more the amount of light in the residential units, the higher the level of happiness of the residents. In a way, it seems that the optimal and purposeful design of daylight in the living space is effective in improving the mental health of people and the happiness of the residents.

Embracing the Divine: The Symbolism of the Sacred in Dreams

The sacred in dreams symbolizes our connection to the divine, the depth of our spiritual beliefs, and the reverence we hold for transcendent truths. These dreams reflect our innermost yearnings for spiritual connection, the challenges of understanding and embracing spiritual truths, and the opportunities for growth and enlightenment through the exploration of the sacred. The imagery of a glowing light enveloping an ancient symbol or artifact evokes a sense of awe, the mystery of the divine, and the beauty of spiritual discovery, illustrating how dreams of the sacred can reflect our fears, aspirations, and the pursuit of understanding and embracing the profound aspects of our spirituality and existence.

Divine Connection: The sacred represents our yearning for a connection with the divine, emphasizing the pursuit of spiritual union and the deep bonds we seek with higher powers.

Spiritual Beliefs: It symbolizes the depth and complexity of our spiritual beliefs, reflecting our quest for understanding and the significance we ascribe to spiritual truths.

Transcendence and Reverence: Dreams of the sacred underscore our reverence for that which transcends ordinary understanding, highlighting the awe and respect we hold for the mysteries of existence and the spiritual journey.

Psychological Perspective on the Sacred in Dreams

Psychologically, the sacred in dreams can mirror our subconscious explorations of spirituality, our attitudes towards the divine, and our intrinsic need for meaning and connection beyond the material world. They may indicate our inner conflicts, aspirations for enlightenment, and the emotional and intellectual engagement with the transcendent aspects of life.

Cultural Interpretations of Dreaming About the Sacred

Culturally, the sacred is often intertwined with religious practices, spiritual traditions, and the collective search for meaning, symbolizing the universal human quest for understanding the divine and the moral and ethical frameworks derived from spiritual beliefs. Dreams about the sacred can thus reflect cultural narratives around divinity, the diversity of spiritual expressions, and the personal significance of engaging with sacred concepts and symbols.

Spiritual Meanings of the Sacred in Dreams

Spiritually, the sacred in dreams might signify the soul's journey, the communication with higher realms, and the quest for spiritual awakening. They can represent the inner call to explore spiritual paths, the challenges of spiritual growth, and the transformative power of encountering the sacred within the self and the universe.

How to Interpret Your Sacred Dreams

Examine the Sacred Symbol or Artifact: The specific symbol or artifact enveloped in light—its historical, cultural, or spiritual significance—can offer insights into the aspects of spirituality you are exploring or the divine messages being conveyed.

Consider the Context: The context in which the sacred appears—solitary contemplation, a ritual, an ethereal landscape—can shed light on your spiritual journey, the nature of your quest for connection, and your feelings about the divine and transcendence.

Reflect on Your Emotions: Your emotional response to the sacred in the dream can reveal your subconscious feelings about spirituality, your yearnings for divine connection, and your attitudes towards the mysteries and challenges of spiritual exploration.

War in a dream

According to the interpretation of Ibn Sirin, seeing war in a dream always denotes calamities, and adversities, except for those whose work is related to war, such as soldiers, arms makers, and army leaders.

Interpretation of seeing war in a dream by Ibn Sirin

Ibn Sirin says that war in a dream indicates public or private adversities, and seeing war in a dream symbolizes a severe calamity facing the seer and the worries that control him. This symbolizes a good conclusion, and Allah Almighty knows best.

War in a dream indicates the prevailing calamity, except for those whose work is in the affairs of war and weapons, and the dream of war also indicates diseases and epidemics, and war in a dream for a married woman symbolizes the many worries and increasing problems with her husband or with parents.

Ibn Sirin distinguishes between three forms of seeing war in a dream that is worthy of interpretation. The first is that the war in a dream is between two sultanates or two armies, and in this case, the war is a calamity, general disease, and sedition.

As for the second form, the war in the dream is between the sultans and the common people, which then indicate the cheapness and the low price of food.

As for the third and final form, the war in the dream is between the subjects, meaning seeing the civil war in a dream, which indicates sedition and high food prices, and Allah knows best.

Seeing war in a dream denotes high prices and cheapness according to its accidents and parties in the dream, and war in a dream indicates quarrels between people and between countries, and wars in dreams may be a sign of the spread of diseases.

The war in the dream, according to the interpretation of Dr. Suleiman Al-Dulaimi, indicates devastation, destruction, and disintegration, and this is reflected in the affairs of the dreamer. Victory in war may mean victory in old conflicts, as well as defeat in war in a dream may indicate a near failure.

Interpretation of seeing war in a dream by Sheikh Nabulsi

Sheikh Al-Nabulsi said, "War in a dream indicates deception and cunning, and seeing people fight each other in a dream is evidence of high prices and distress Allah knows.

Sheikh Nabulsi adds in the chapter on fighting in a dream; He saw himself fighting the people of falsehood and the oppressor in a dream, and his conscience is that he is with the people of truth, and then this is a victory for the religion and the parents.

Interpretation of seeing war in a dream by Ibn Shaheen

Ibn Shaheen says that if the war in a dream is between kings, it indicates the spread of strife, and whoever sees the war between the king and people, this may indicate a drop in commodity prices, and as for seeing civil wars in a dream, it may indicate the opposite, and Allah knows best, and the closest to be predominant in a dream of war defeated in reality, losing a war in a dream is a profit in reality, and making peace in a dream or a truce is a sign of a general good, Allah willing.

And seeing war in a dream for those in power is an actual war and calamity on people and the warrior has victory and dominion over him.

War in a dream is for a farmer plowing his land because he hits it with machines that resemble war machines, and war for a prisoner in a dream is that he plans to escape, and for the sick, he is suffering from his illness, and for the believer, he is fighting evil, and war for the sinner is that he is fighting obedience, and Allah knows best.

Interpretation of seeing a war between two countries in a dream for single women

War in a dream for single women indicates defiance of society, customs, and traditions, and seeing a war between two countries in a dream for single women indicates the struggle and quarrel between her parents, and the dream of participating in the war for singles indicates the entry into an immoral matter of strife and intrigue.

Interpretation of a dream about war and missiles for a single woman indicates quick events in her life and major changes, and hearing the sound of bombing and missiles in the dream for the single woman indicates the anxiety and fear that she suffers from, and going down to shelters in the dream indicates the trade-in someone who protects her.

Interpretation of a dream about a war for a married woman

Seeing war in a dream for a married woman indicates many quarrels and disagreements in her family.

A war between two countries in a dream for a married woman symbolizes a dispute between her senior families or a dispute between her family and her husband's family. Seeing war between two countries in a dream may symbolize the psychological conflict experienced by the viewer between two options, and whoever saw a war in her country in a dream indicates high prices or general strife, Allah knows.

As for the one who sees one of her family dying in the war, they enter into the trials of this world and forget the afterlife, and if the married woman sees that she dies in the war in a dream, then she loses a rivalry, and the death in the war of the married woman indicates her corruption and misguidance.

Fleeing from the war in a dream for a married woman indicates her retirement from sedition and non-interference in a family problem, and escaping from the war in a dream indicates her deliverance from danger and evil.

Interpretation of a dream about war, bombing, and missiles

Seeing war and bombing in a dream indicates sudden, frightening, and accelerating events. Perhaps the dream of bombing is a symbol of the anxiety and tension experienced by the dream owner.

The bombing of missiles in a dream indicates events that cause tension and anxiety, and missiles in a dream are symbols that indicate quick and successive matters, good or evil, according to the evidence of the vision.

Fear of bombing in a dream symbolizes safety from strife if the dreamer is not harmed, and the interpretation of escaping from bombing in a dream that it indicates avoiding strife or withdrawing from verbal arguments and problems, and surviving from missile bombing in the dream indicates an exit from successive crises.

Hearing the sound of bombing and missiles in a dream indicates hearing shocking and sudden news, and whoever sees that he hears the sound of bombing in a dream while he is in a safe place, indicates that he has been saved from something he hears about and does not witness danger.

Interpretation of a dream about a war with planes

The dream of war with planes indicates intense competition in work and livelihood, and whoever sees warplane fighting in the sky in the dream indicates a great struggle in his work over positions and promotions, and it was said that planes war in a dream indicates sedition between rulers and politicians, and Allah knows best.

Participation in the war of planes in a dream symbolizes the quest to achieve victory in the competition, and whoever sees that he is driving a warplane in a dream, will reach his goals quickly, or this vision indicates the superiority of the seer over his peers in the rivalry.

Bombing planes in a dream indicates affliction from the sky, and whoever sees planes bombed randomly in a dream, may symbolize public calamities.

Interpretation of war with Israel in a dream

War with Israel in a dream indicates the emergence of severe enmity in the life of the seer, and victory in the war with Israel in a dream symbolizes the victory of truth over falsehood and the elevation of the word of truth. As for defeat in front of Israel in a war in a dream, it indicates the victory of falsehood and the victory of injustice.

And whoever sees that he is fighting on the side of Israel in a dream, then he is breaking a promise or betraying his friend, and this will bring him back sedition and worry, and seeing death in the war with Israel in the dream symbolizes sincere repentance and a good end.

It was said that war with Israel in a dream is one of the symbols that indicate facing injustice and entering into conflicts with the oppressors and the tyrants.

Seeing the bombing of Israel in a dream indicates telling the truth without fear.

And seeing the bombing from Israel in the dream indicates the general strife and problems between people, and Allah knows best.

Seeing ancient wars and invasions of Muslims in a dream

Seeing war between Muslims in a dream symbolizes great strife, but whoever sees a war between Muslims and non-Muslims in the dream, it is the war between truth and falsehood, and the victory of one over the other in a dream indicates a large number of people of truth or a large number of people of falsehood, the victory of Muslims in a war in a dream indicates Right over wrong.

And whoever dreams that he is witnessing one of the conquests of Muslims in a dream, and then is searching for truth and guidance.

And whoever dreams that he is fighting with the Muslim army in a dream, this indicates the sincerity of faith and standing by the truth. Perhaps this dream denotes a testimony that the seer witnesses before a judge. As for seeing war with the infidels in the dream and the seer on their side, this indicates the victory of falsehood over the truth, and Allah is Most Exalted and All-Knowing.

Seeing wars with swords in a dream indicates that the word of truth is exalted and standing by it.

Interpretation of seeing participation in war in a dream

Whoever dreams that he is witnessing a war while he is not in it, then sees sedition and does not enter it, and participating in the war in a dream indicates the entry of the dreamer into strife or conflict. That he is with the corrupt party, he is an outrageous aggressor who weakens people.

And whoever sees that he leads a war in a dream then ignites sedition or invents something, and the leadership of the war in the dream may indicate decisive decisions in work and personal life.

And seeing the participation of street war in a dream indicates strife between people, and street war in a dream may symbolize the injustice and oppression of the rulers, and Ibn Sirin said seeing civil war in a dream is an indication of the high prices.

Interpretation of war tools in a dream

Seeing the sword in a dream, in general, denotes offensive speech. Seeing war clothes in a dream indicates the rate of temptation.

War shields in a dream indicates protection from temptation, and a warrior's helmet in a dream indicates discussion, arguments, and proof.

And the interpretation of seeing guns or tools of modern individual warfare may refer to a war of words and ideas, and war trenches in a dream indicate cunning and deception of people.

As for the one who sees him driving a tank or a military vehicle in the war, if he is a soldier, then he is one of Allah's soldiers, and if he is not, he will refrain from fuelling sedition.

Seeing the radar in a dream indicates the spy and the voyeur, and whoever sees that he operates the radar in a dream, is following people's news. As for seeing the radar on the roof in the dream, it indicates the release of the secrets of the seer's house into the open.

A symbol of escaping from the war in a dream

Fleeing from the war in a dream indicates intense fear of confrontation or competition. Fleeing from the war in a dream denotes that the dreamer abandons his rights and abandons them.

Seeing soldiers escaping from the war in a dream symbolizes the corruption of people and rulers and high prices, and whoever sees enemy soldiers escaping from the war in a dream, indicates the return of rights to its people and the end of great strife.

Interpretation of a dream about death in war

Seeing death in war indicates the pursuit of sedition or heresy, and death in war was said in a dream if the owner of the dream was fighting with the people of truth, this indicates a good conclusion or facing falsehood, and the dream of martyrdom in war indicates acceptance of supplication and response as it indicates sincere repentance.

As for whoever sees one of his family in a dream dying in war, this may indicate his distance from the truth if he is a sinner and his good conclusion if he is a righteous person, and the death of a brother in war in a dream symbolizes his being dragged into fitnah or falling into a calamity, as well as the death of a sister, father or mother.

Seeing the dead fighting in a dream symbolizes the emergence of new hopes in the life of the seer, and whoever sees the dead fighting each other in the dream is hitting the unjust with the unjust. After he died in the war, it symbolizes the return of the stolen right to its owner.

Prisoners of war in a dream

Whoever sees in a dream that he is captured in a war may be imprisoned by an unjust sultan, and falling into the captivity of the enemy in the dream may indicate a price increase that pervades the country. So on renewed hostility.

As for the killing of prisoners in a dream, it indicates arbitrariness and intransigence, and if the killing was by shooting in a dream, this may indicate words of the same type as the act, and the execution of prisoners of war in a dream is the destruction of weak and poor people because of corruption and injustice.

Interpretation of the end of the war in a dream

The end of the war in a dream is generally good and correct, as Allah Almighty says in Surat Al-Ma'idah ((Whenever they kindled a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it)).
